high.title: Brazil Set to Be First Target of New Round of Trump Tariffs; 25% Rate Could Hit 4,000 Products
high.summary: According to four sources cited by Reuters who are closely following the negotiations, Brazil is bracing for the imposition of a new 25% tariff by the United States that could affect more than 4,000 Brazilian products. Brazil is reportedly expected to be the first target in a new wave of tariffs following the U.S. Supreme Court's ruling that struck down the Trump administration's original tariff framework, prompting Washington to pursue a fresh legal avenue for trade pressure. Months of bilateral negotiations have reportedly yielded little progress. This development carries significant macro implications for Brazil: a broad 25% tariff on thousands of exported goods would directly damage Brazil's trade balance, compress export revenues, and weigh heavily on the BRL. For FX traders, this is a material downside risk for the Real, as deteriorating external accounts typically drive capital outflows and currency depreciation. Brazilian government bond yields may rise as the fiscal outlook worsens. Equity investors should monitor export-heavy names. Watch for any official Brazilian government response and whether retaliatory trade measures are considered, as escalation could further unsettle BRL/USD dynamics.

high.title: Markets Monitor Weaker Inflation and Strait of Hormuz Tensions; Ibovespa in Dollar Terms Falls Today (July 15)
high.summary: International markets are operating cautiously on Wednesday amid persistent geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. President Trump walked back a proposal to impose a 20% transit fee on vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz, opting instead to pursue economic cooperation with Gulf nations through investment agreements. Despite the softer tone, the regional situation remains fragile. The Ibovespa, measured in U.S. dollar terms, is declining on the day, reflecting a combination of global risk-off sentiment and BRL weakness. Weaker-than-expected inflation data (likely U.S. CPI) is also in focus for market participants, as it could influence Fed rate expectations and global capital flows, with downstream effects on emerging market currencies including BRL. For Brazilian fixed income traders, the interplay between global disinflation signals and local geopolitical risk warrants close attention. The dollar-denominated decline in the Ibovespa underscores currency headwinds that international fund managers with unhedged Brazil exposure must monitor carefully.

medium.title: No Improvement in Sight: BTG Sees Another Difficult Quarter for Brazilian Retail; Which Stocks May Stand Out
medium.summary:
BTG Pactual is flagging Q2 2026 as another challenging quarter for Brazilian retail, citing no meaningful improvement in the macroeconomic backdrop. Elevated Selic rates continue to erode household disposable income, while high family indebtedness and cumulative inflation keep consumer purchasing power under pressure. Although this article focuses on the retail sector rather than macro directly, BTG's commentary is relevant as a real-economy signal: persistently high interest rates are transmitting meaningfully into consumption, reinforcing that the current monetary tightening cycle is having its intended contractionary effect. For bond and rate traders, this supports the narrative that the Selic is biting — a factor the BCB will weigh in future COPOM deliberations. Watch whether softening consumption data begins to build a case for an earlier-than-expected rate cut pivot.
